flashcards.q: What is the core architectural split in Trino?
flashcards.a: One coordinator (parse, plan, optimize, schedule splits, track memory) plus stateless workers that execute splits; stages connect via local/remote exchanges; connectors bind sources as catalogs.

flashcards.q: Presto vs Trino vs Athena lineage?
flashcards.a: Presto built 2012 at Facebook, open sourced 2013; creators forked to PrestoSQL 2018; renamed Trino Dec 2020 after the Facebook/Linux Foundation trademark dispute. AWS Athena engine v2 was Presto 0.217; engine v3 is Trino-based.
Stage = one parallelized fragment of the plan; split = unit of work inside a stage (roughly one connector chunk: file stripe or predicate-pushed scan range). Workers run many splits concurrently.

flashcards.q: How does federation actually move data?
flashcards.a: Connectors declare capabilities; the optimizer pushes predicates/projections/aggregations/topN down to capable sources; whatever cannot be absorbed crosses the network through exchanges into worker memory.

flashcards.q: Name the three memory categories and their enforcement.
flashcards.a: User memory (blocking-operator state; hard per-node/per-query limits, fail-fast EXCEEDED_MEMORY_LIMIT), revocable memory (spillable to disk under cluster pressure), system memory (tracked internal buffers/exchange queues).

join.distribution-type=AUTOMATIC: broadcast build side if estimated under join.broadcast-threshold (~100MB), else partitioned hash join shuffling both sides. Underestimated broadcast = classic OOM generator; stats matter.

flashcards.q: How many times does a CTE referenced 3 times execute?
flashcards.a: Treat it as three executions: CTEs historically inline like macros; newer releases improve reuse but verify in EXPLAIN before trusting it. N references = N scans until proven otherwise.

flashcards.q: Materialized views in OSS Trino: what works, what doesn't?
flashcards.a: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW over Hive/Iceberg/Delta stores results as a table and rewrites eligible queries transparently; refresh is explicit REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW -- no scheduler, no auto-refresh in OSS (commercial distros add it). No general result cache exists in OSS.

Exchange manager persists stage intermediates to S3/HDFS so a lost worker's splits retry from checkpointed state instead of failing/restarting the whole query. Landed experimentally early 2023; extends Trino into long batch territory previously owned by Spark.

flashcards.q: When is federated query an anti-pattern?
flashcards.a: Hot-path OLTP sources absorbing analytics load; row-level lookups paying MPP startup latency; high-cardinality joins pushdown can't shrink; cross-region compliance violations; anything needing cross-source transactional consistency.

flashcards.q: Why do small files hurt Trino badly and what fixes them?
flashcards.a: Every file becomes a split with open/read/close overhead plus metadata listing; millions of small files make planning dominate runtime. Fix at table-format layer: OPTIMIZE/compaction to ~128MB targets, manifest rewrite, partition alignment with real predicates.

flashcards.q: Athena pricing model and its lever?
flashcards.a: Serverless, ~$5 per TB scanned; cost is governed entirely by scan discipline -- partitioning, Parquet/columnar formats, predicate selectivity translate directly to dollars.
